title: fix(plugin-calendar,i18n): route ObjectCalendar's user-visible copy through the locale packs
body:
Fixes #10031

Clause-②: no — adding keys to the English pack and routing four literals through hooks the component already imports. It relaxes no accept set and widens no public surface.

⚠️ That line is copied verbatim from the claim comment, and **two of its figures moved under measurement**. Both corrections are in this body: the sweep found **twelve** sites, not four, and the keys land in **all ten packs**, not in the English one alone. The clause's verdict is unchanged and re-checked: no accept set is relaxed, no published surface widens.

Drafted by an ObjectUI development agent seat (Claude Code), session `session_018HrVaotisyhgmot9o2MLRq`. Every figure below was re-derived on this branch.

## 1. The instrument first — the card corrected its own, and the correction holds

The filing seat recorded that it had once counted the translation calls in this file with a bare `t(` and reported 15, then retracted that number because the pattern also matches every word ending in `t`. Re-derived here, on this very file, with a control in the same command:

| pattern | what it matches on `ObjectCalendar.tsx` |
|:--|:--|
| `t\(` (the retracted one) | 12 lines — `useEffect(`, `handleDateClickDefault(`, `e.preventDefault(` and the three real calls |
| `\btt?\(` (word boundary, optional doubled `t`) | 3 occurrences, and nothing else |

The disciplined pattern needs the optional second `t`: `\bt\(` alone matches only the single-`t` hook and silently drops both `tt(` calls — one occurrence, which reads like a *different* wrong answer. Run against a five-line control file holding the three decoys plus the two real shapes, the bare pattern claims five lines and the disciplined one claims exactly the two real calls.

⇒ **the card's corrected figure of 3 is confirmed**: two `tt(...)` through `useSafeTranslate` and one `t(...)` through `useObjectTranslation`.

## 2. The literal sweep — four was a lower bound, and the card said so

Swept by three passes over the whole component (quoted literals carrying a space, user-visible JSX attributes, and a read of the entire render tree), not by re-reading the card's list. **Twelve sites**, of which the card named four:

| # | site | literal | on the card? |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| 1 | loading screen | `Loading calendar...` | yes |
| 2 | error screen | the `Error:` prefix | yes |
| 3 | refusal screen, paragraph one | `Calendar configuration required. …` | yes |
| 4 | refusal screen, paragraph two | `It belongs on the view's calendar block. …` | yes (same bullet) |
| 5 | record overlay title, both arms | `Event Details` twice | yes |
| 6 | pull-to-refresh, idle | `Pull to refresh` | **no** |
| 7 | pull-to-refresh, active | `Refreshing…` | **no** |
| 8 | quick-create dialog title | `New event` | **no** |
| 9 | quick-create date line | the `On ` prefix | **no** |
| 10 | quick-create field label | `Title` | **no** |
| 11 | quick-create placeholder | `What's this event about?` | **no** |
| 12 | quick-create buttons | `Cancel`, `Create`, `Creating…` | **no** |
| 13 | quick-create validation | `Title is required` | **no** |

All thirteen rows are repaired (row 12 is three literals in two buttons, which is why the site count reads twelve). Three of them needed no new key at all: `calendar.newEvent`, `common.cancel` and `common.create` already carried exactly these words in all ten packs.

⛔ **One thing deliberately NOT changed**: the text of the underlying error in row 2. The prefix is this component's copy and moves; the message beside it is the thrower's own string — a server diagnostic, or this file's own `DataSource required for object/api providers` — and translating it here would be this component claiming authorship of text it did not write. The key is `Error: {{message}}` and the hole is passed through verbatim.

## 3. Which hook per site, and why — one criterion, and the file already stated it

The card explicitly declined to rule this, and the component's own comment beside its existing `t()` call already carries the deciding fact: `useSafeTranslate` returns `tt(keyOrKeys, fallback)` and **passes no options to i18next**, so it cannot fill an interpolation hole.

⇒ **a site with a hole uses `t()`; every hole-free site uses `tt()`.** That is two sites on `t()` — the error prefix (`{{message}}`) and the quick-create date line (`{{date}}`) — and ten on `tt()`. No site was decided on taste.

## 4. ⚠️ The route the card offered is not available, and here is the measurement

The card suggested — explicitly as a suggestion, not a ruling — that only `packages/i18n/src/locales/en.ts` need change, because the English fallback carries the English text so the other nine packs need not follow.

**The English fallback does carry the call site. It does not carry the key set.** The key-set invariant in this repo is a pack-versus-pack one: every pack defines every `en` key, and no pack defines a key `en` lacks, with a single documented exemption set that this card is not in. It is answered by the packs, and no fallback at a call site is visible to it.

Measured, by ablation, with the mutation and the restore both proven on disk by object hash rather than by an exit code: with the twelve keys present in `en` and reverted out of the other nine, `all-locales-key-parity.test.ts` fails **nine** cases, each naming the same twelve keys. Restored, the nine pack files are byte-identical to their committed blobs and the working tree is clean.

Two independent confirmations of the same reading, neither of them my own reasoning:

- `pnpm check:i18n-drift` prints the ownership itself for this branch — it reports the twelve as *added* keys and says in its own words that additions belong to the key-parity test, not to it.
- **PR #10091, the hot file this card was queued behind, is the worked example**: it adds ONE key and its file list carries all ten locale packs.

⇒ this branch adds the twelve keys to all ten packs, with real translations rather than the English value — a value byte-identical to `en` inside a non-Latin pack is itself a defect this repo's suite reds on. Nine of the ten pack files are therefore outside the file surface the dispatch drew, and that surface was drawn from the route this section falsifies. It is declared rather than quietly taken, and it is in the report to the PM as an open question.

## 5. One rendered English string moved, on purpose

`Loading calendar...` now renders `Loading calendar…` — three ASCII full stops became U+2026. Not a style choice: the sentence is now a pack value, and every pack value in this repo is held to the typographic ellipsis by `ellipsis-glyph-3878.test.ts`. The one suite that pinned the ASCII spelling (`ObjectCalendar.recordSourceMembers-8314.test.tsx`, its `LOADING_PLACEHOLDER` constant) moves with it and says why at the constant.

⭐ **The refusal screen's English is byte-identical to what it rendered before**, both paragraphs, apostrophes included — which is what keeps the five suites that pin that screen green without touching any of them.

## 6. Evidence

**RED before, GREEN after, with the file state read in the same command as each run.** The new pin is `ObjectCalendar.localizedSurface-10031.test.tsx`. It mounts the component under `zh` and asserts each string is **not** its English literal — an English-locale assertion on the English text passes identically on both trees, because a hard-coded sentence and a pack value carrying the same sentence render the same bytes.

- against the pre-repair component, proven on disk to be the base blob and to contain zero routed call sites: **7 failed, 1 passed**. The one that passes is the locale probe — the control that says the harness really loaded `zh`, so every "the English literal is gone" zero below it is a reading rather than a broken provider.
- after the repair: **8 passed**.
- restored: the component is byte-identical to its committed blob, `git diff HEAD` empty, `git status` empty.

**Package suites**, repo-root invocation: `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-calendar/ packages/i18n/` — **108 files, 1436 tests, all passing**, including key parity, the ellipsis glyph rule, the Arabic participle orthography rule, the untranslated-identity sweep and the five refusal-screen pins.

**Type-check**: `@object-ui/plugin-calendar` and `@object-ui/i18n`, both legs of each package's `type-check` script (the `--noEmit` pass and the test-config pass), after building the dependency closure of both packages. Exit 0.

**Lint**: both affected packages' own `lint` scripts, over the 144 files eslint's own configuration selects in them — 0 errors. The remaining warnings are the pre-existing `no-explicit-any` population these files already carried. The narrowing to those two packages is safe to state rather than assume: this repo's eslint configuration enables no type-aware linting, so no edit in this diff can move the verdict on a file it does not touch.

## 7. Gates

Run as the last action before the push, on the committed tree with nothing unstaged.

| gate | exit | does it select this diff? |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `check:i18n-keys` | 0 | **yes** — it resolves every call site against the `en` pack; its own summary reports the full population it walked, not a collapsed one |
| `check:i18n-drift` | 0 | **yes** — and it names this branch's twelve additions and states they are key parity's business |
| `check:i18n-dead-keys` | 0 | **yes**, but report-only and wired into no workflow; none of the twelve new keys appears in its candidate list |
| `check:i18n-designer-parity` | 0 | **no** — its corpus is the metadata-admin designer's module-local tables, which this diff does not touch. Green here is not a statement about this change |
| `check:control-bytes` | 0 | yes, whole tree |
| `check:new-line-citations` | 0 | yes — 0 new cross-file line addresses |
| `check-changeset-presence` | 0 | yes — decided by running it, not from memory: it reported 12 published source files of 2 released packages and refused until the changeset existed |
| `check-changeset-no-major` | 0 | yes |
| `check-governed-queue-guard --test` | 0 | yes — 14 paths checked, none governed |

No gate answered `PRECONDITION NOT MET`, and no population read as collapsed.

## 8. The hot file

⚠️ **Rewritten by the accepting seat at 2026-09-20T16:23Z. The paragraph this replaces asserted something that is now FALSE about `main`, and a squash lands this body verbatim in `main`'s commit log — so a dated figure may stay, but a false claim may not.** The original reading, as taken at push time, was: `packages/i18n/src/locales/en.ts` re-checked against `origin/main`, PR #10091 not landed and its key absent, `origin/main` two commits past this branch's base touching neither package.

**What actually happened.** Both of the changes that paragraph treated as hypothetical landed while this PR was parked behind incident objectui#10148, and this branch has since merged `origin/main` (`cbda340f0`) in — merge commit `2c9f6e265`, a true merge with two parents, ⛔ no rebase and ⛔ no force-push, verified by the accepting seat: `3b91e84f9` (the old head) and `cbda340f0` are each an ancestor of it.

- **objectui#10091 has landed**, as `3ac2de829`. Its `console.studio` block is in all ten packs; git auto-merged it in a different region and the resolution left it byte-identical. `apps/console/src/components/StudioRoute.landingI18n.test.tsx`, which reads exactly those keys, passes.
- **objectui#10142 has landed**, as `f760064ea` — and it, ⛔ not #10091, is what this branch actually conflicted with. It added a nested `calendar.a11y` sub-object to the tail of the same `calendar` block these twelve flat keys append to. One hunk per pack, ten packs, identical shape.
- **Resolved as a union**, ours then theirs, keeping the nested block last where `main` placed it; zero key-name overlap was checked per pack first, so the union creates no duplicate property.

⭐ Verified by the accepting seat on its own instrument rather than accepted from the report: `git diff --numstat cbda340f0 2c9f6e265 -- packages/i18n/src/locales/` reads **ten files, +120/−0** — twelve keys times ten packs, and **zero deletions**, so nothing `main` carried was dropped in the resolution.

The section's closing advice stands and was followed: the key-parity suite was re-run after the merge, green.

## Acceptance notes

Found while sweeping, **reported and not fixed here** — neither is in this card's fence:

- ~~**`CalendarView`'s own accessibility copy is hard-coded English** — its region label, its grid label and its today button's label. Same defect class as this card, one file over, and that file is outside the declared surface.~~ ✅ **No longer open — struck by the accepting seat at 2026-09-20T16:23Z.** objectui#10142 fixed it on `main` (commit `f760064ea`), routing those accessible names through these same packs, and its `calendar.a11y` block is what this branch merged in. Its pin `CalendarView.a11yLabelsLocalized-10104` — including its lit control that `zh` differs from `en` for every swept key — runs green on the merged tree. ⛔ Struck rather than deleted: it was a true finding when written, and this PR's history is the record of that.
- **`ObjectCalendar`'s pull-to-refresh gesture is dead on the internal-fetch path.** `usePullToRefresh` attaches its native listeners in a mount effect whose dependencies are all stable for this component, and on that path the first render is the loading screen — so the ref is null when the effect runs and the listeners are never attached at all. Reproduced while writing the pin: driving the gesture through the internal-fetch path produces nothing, and the same gesture through pre-fetched `data` (where the first render already mounts the host) works. The pin therefore reaches the affordance through pre-fetched data, and says at the assertion that it is routing around a separate defect rather than hiding one.
